dedupe_keys.name: the deadly choices at memorial evacuation of memorial medical center after hurricane katrina propublica

description: A long investigative article by Sheri Fink, published by ProPublica on 27 August 2009, reconstructing the days after Hurricane Katrina at Memorial Medical Center in Uptown New Orleans. The hospital sat three feet below sea level; about 2,000 people sheltered in it, including more than 200 patients and 600 workers. The hurricane cut power and running water, generators built to run only emergency lights, critical equipment and a few outlets failed, air conditioning stopped and temperatures passed 100 degrees F. Helicopters landed on an old helipad atop an eight-storey parking garage but too slowly; the patient count fell from 187 to about 130 while 52 patients of the LifeCare unit on the seventh floor, seven on ventilators, remained. The account follows staff decisions on who to evacuate first, how scarce resources were shared, the deaths that followed and the later grand jury decision. Coverage: one hospital and one week. Access: free web article; it is journalism, not a data release, and depends on interviews. Useful as a detailed case for hospital emergency response, backup power and evacuation planning. It relates to the Urban Institute report on New Orleans hospitals in the catalogue.
